mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances following RSAFS increases, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals a weakening supply side, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies face reduced output and potential earnings shortfalls.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% year-over-year and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of high CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4%, it signals a strong labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS growth and low UNRATE on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strong demand for new homes, which boosts related industries and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances following HOUST increases, or if the correlation between HOUST growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth slows to less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1% over the same period, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the joint effect of GDPC1 slowdown and INDPRO decline on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
